title: Runtime signal thermometer and request catalog — Jul 2026
summary: Compact synthesis of field reports about runtime latency patterns, KV/prefix cache behavior, and a prioritized catalog of small-to-medium engineering patches requested by customers. This doc focuses on concrete remediations that unblock mid-market customers running bursty workflows.
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, field-driven snapshot intended to translate customer frustration (latency spikes, cache misses, opaque routing) into a prioritized set of actionable asks. Target audience: product managers, serving-runtime engineers, SREs, and solutions engineering.

Topline signal (thermometer):
- Cool: features working as expected in steady-state, P50 token latency ~30–60ms for typical chat workloads.
- Warm: occasional prefix cache cold starts drive P95 into 300–700ms ranges for clients with varied prompt templates.
- Hot: under certain multi-tenant bursts (large batch fan-out + long contexts), we see P95/P99 spikes 700ms–1.2s and increased retry rates; several customers reported user-visible timeouts.

Representative customer vignettes and asks:
1) AcmeRetail (large embedding+reranking pipeline):
   - Symptom: periodic tail latency causing downstream inference timeouts in search re-rank step.
   - Observed telemetry: batch size oscillation during their hourly ingest + 28% KV cache miss rate.
   - Ask: offer a tenant-level knob for burst routing (route to a warmed pool) and export per-tenant cache hit-rate.
   - Suggested priority: P1 (business visible).

2) FinSight (sensitive private deployment, on Dedicated):
   - Symptom: P95 spikes correlated with model quantization fallback on older nodes.
   - Observed telemetry: node-type mismatch in routing policy; fallback adds 150–400ms per request.
   - Ask: expose automatic compatibility mapping in console (explain when a fallback will be used) and a per-deployment compatibility report.
   - Suggested priority: P1.

3) MakerBot (PLG startup, hosted API):
   - Symptom: developers see unpredictable latency for interactive demos; perceived as flakiness.
   - Observed telemetry: high prefix variance between tenants; short-lived sessions have low effective cache reuse.
   - Ask: lightweight client SDK guidance + default warmup micro-requests for new sessions; optional SDK warmup helper.
   - Suggested priority: P2 (developer UX).

Small/medium engineering asks (catalog):
- Telemetry: add a per-tenant "prefix-hit-rate" timeseries and a dashboard tile that surfaces cold-start percent by hour. (effort: small; owner: observability)
- Runtime: honor a "preferred_pool" routing hint in request headers to force assignment to warmed pools for a short window. (effort: medium; owner: routing)
- Console: create an automated "compatibility report" that flags model/VM mismatches that will cause quantization or kernel fallbacks. (effort: small; owner: console)
- SDK: add a 1-line warmup helper for single-session demos (micro-batched trivial prompts to populate KV cache). (effort: small; owner: devexp)
- Cost/behavior note: adding forced warm pools increases cost if adopted widely; recommend feature gated with tenant opt-in + cost-estimate shown in console.

Quick wins (0–2 weeks):
- Hook an existing prefix-hit metric into the CS runbook alerting so we can call customers proactively when a sustained cold period is detected.
- Add a short snippet for SDK warmup to the quickstart and email to MakerBot PO.

Medium work (2–8 weeks):
- Prototype "preferred_pool" header in a canary and run against one willing customer (AcmeRetail). Monitor unit economics for that tenant.
- Console compatibility report + link to the tenant's routing policy and node types.

Risk flags and unresolved questions:
- Risk: Preferred_pool could be abused to hog warmed capacity; need quota and decay semantics (TTL on warm assignment).
- Question: how to price warmed-pool bursts? Per-minute premium, or fixed hourly reservation? Lean toward per-minute for trial.
- Risk: exposing detailed node-type behavior increases support surface (customers might demand specific instance types).

Suggested owners and next steps (short runbook):
- Obs: Marco Ruiz — add prefix-hit-rate dashboard tile and hook to CS alerts (ETA 1w).
- Routing: Leah Chen — design header semantics + decay TTL and implement canary API (ETA 3–6w).
- Console: Omar Siddiqui — compatibility report mockup (ETA 2w).
- CS / Solutions Eng: Aisha Patel — coordinate AcmeRetail pilot and craft customer comms (ETA 1w to reach pilot agreement).

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Consider a small A/B test where we charge small premium for warmed pool vs free warmup helper — gives data on willingness to pay.
- Capture any PR/issue numbers during canary and paste into this doc for handoff.
- Slack threads: #cs-acme-retail, #runtime-latency.

Appendix (raw customer quotes):
- "Sometimes the demo just stalls; it's the worst first impression." — MakerBot eng lead.
- "We see spikes right after our daily batch runs; it's like the system forgets us." — AcmeRetail infra.

If accepted: propose a 6-week pilot plan (observability + routing canary + one customer) and a light comms template for pilot participants.

-- end of note --
